Pinhole leak in the master bathroom supply line, resulting from

SCOPE OF INSPECTION

Inspection conducted in response to claim filed 04/15/2023 for water
damage originating from the master bathroom supply line. Insured
reported the leak was discovered on 04/14/2023 when he returned from
work. Water had spread to the master bedroom ceiling and carpet.

OBSERVATIONS

1. MASTER BATHROOM
   - Supply line under sink had a visible pinhole leak approx. 2 inches
     from the shut-off valve. Corrosion noted on the valve body.
   - Shut-off valve was seized; could not be fully closed at time of
     inspection. Insured stated he had turned off the main water supply
     after discovering the leak.
   - Flooring (vinyl) showed minor water staining near the vanity;
     no lifting or delamination observed.
   - No damage to vanity cabinet; base was dry at time of inspection.

2. MASTER BEDROOM
   - Ceiling: water stain approx. 4 ft x 3 ft, centered near the
     bathroom wall. Drywall was sagging in one spot (approx. 12" x 8").
     Measured moisture content with pin meter: 18% at the sagging area,
     12% at the edge of the stain.
   - Carpet: damp along the wall adjacent to the bathroom. Padding
     saturated in a strip approx. 3 ft wide. Carpet was pulled back in
     one corner by the insured for drying; no mold odor detected.
   - Baseboards: minor swelling at the joint near the bathroom door.

3. OTHER AREAS
   - Hallway outside master bedroom: no visible water damage. Carpet
     dry.
   - Living room, kitchen, other bedrooms: no damage observed.

4. EXTERIOR
   - No evidence of roof or siding leaks. Water source confirmed to be
     the bathroom supply line.

CAUSE OF LOSS

Pinhole leak in the master bathroom supply line, resulting from
corrosion. No evidence of freezing, sudden pipe burst, or sewer backup.
The leak was slow and continuous, consistent with the insured's
discovery timeline.
